papers.title: Shape optimization in laminar flow with a label-guided variational autoencoder
papers.abstract: Computational design optimization in fluid dynamics usually requires to solve non-linear partial differential equations numerically. In this work, we explore a Bayesian optimization approach to minimize an object's drag coefficient in laminar flow based on predicting drag directly from the object shape. Jointly training an architecture combining a variational autoencoder mapping shapes to latent representations and Gaussian process regression allows us to generate improved shapes in the two dimensional case we consider.

llm.why_not_core: No constraints handling, no uncertainty quantification beyond GP variance, and no biomechanics or implant context.

summary_zh.result: 生成的二维形状显著降低了阻力系数。

summary_en.motivation: The paper aims to minimize drag in laminar flow using Bayesian optimization to avoid repeatedly solving expensive PDEs for each candidate shape.
summary_en.method: A variational autoencoder (VAE) maps shapes to a latent space, on which Gaussian process regression predicts drag, enabling efficient Bayesian optimization.
summary_en.result: The approach generates improved shapes with significantly lower drag compared to the initial designs.
summary_en.validation: The method is validated through numerical simulation of 2D laminar flows.
